description.narrative: SAY Programmet syftar till att förbättra rättigheter, hälsa och ökade möjligheter för ungdomar i utsatta områden. Särskilt fokus ligger på flickor, flyktingar samt barn och ungdomar som befinner sig utanför skolan och utan arbete.

The SAY program aims to improve the rights, health and increased opportunities for young people in vulnerable areas. A special focus is on girls, refugees and children and young people who are out of school and out of work.

The Strengthening Adolescents and Youth Rights and Empowerment Programme - Scaling Impact (SAY Plus) is an expansion of the ongoing SAY Programme (2024-2027), funded by Denmark. With additional funding from Sida for the period 2025-2028, the SAY Plus will geographically expand from the current five districts in the West Nile and Acholi sub-regions to include seven additional districts in the Karamoja and Bukedi sub-regions.
The outcome objective of SAY Plus is to increase access to and utilization of SRHR, HIV and GBV information and services among young people aged 1024 years in underserved regions and communities, including refugee settlements and host- communities in 12 districts in Uganda.
To achieve this, the Programme has defined three key objectives:
1) Creating demand for SRHR/GBV services and information.
2) Building an enabling environment at community and district levels that upholds SRHR, prevents GBV, and supports young people to exercise agency.
3) Strengthening service delivery, including differentiated youth-responsive models.
The Programmes primary beneficiaries are youth aged 1024, particularly adolescent girls and young women. It deliberately includes young persons with disabilities, refugees, in- and out of school youth and other marginalised groups at all stages of implementation, with an aim to promote equitable access to education, health, protection and livelihood opportunities for the underserved. Secondary beneficiaries include parents and guardians, men and boys, cultural, political, and religious leaders, youth leaders, health workers, teachers, women of reproductive age (2549), and policymakers at district, regional, and national levels.

description.narrative:
Output 1: Demand Creation & Adolescent Empowerment
During the reporting period, the programme strengthened the foundations for delivering coordinated, age-appropriate school health and life-skills education. School assessments were completed across Karamoja and Bukedi, and the findings will enable programming to respond to context-specific barriers, while communityfacility referral linkages will improve adolescents' access to accurate information, protection and youth-responsive services. Collectively, these initial investments create a scalable platform for improving learners' health, safety and agency.
Output 2: Enabling Environment & Positive Social Norms (MoGLSD, MoLG, UBOS, NPA) The programme supported the mobilisation of cultural leaders, the embedding of SRHR and GBV indicators in local government accountability systems, improvements in gender-based violence data and response capacity, and the strengthening of national data and planning systems. These investments were aimed at institutionalising multisectoral action, and position both national institutions and local governments to plan, finance and deliver more accountable, evidence-driven services for young people.
Output 3: Differentiated Service Delivery
The programme accelerated differentiated service delivery by combining facility readiness assessments, clinical mentorship and integrated youth-responsive outreach. The quality improvement and emergency obstetric care assessments established the baseline for subsequent health system strengthening, while service delivery expanded adolescents' access to essential SRHR services and established a strong operational platform for equitable, high-quality care in underserved districts.
